newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Spicer-Mitchell issues profit warnings.
newsitem.headline: Spicer-Mitchell issues profit warnings.

text.p: South Africa's Spicer-Mitchell Holdings Ltd and Cityhold warned at the weekend that adverse trading conditions will "negatively affect" interim results due to be published in September.
But group chairman Frits Eloff said he was confident that the worst was over.
The company is due to publish results in September for the six months ended June 30.
Eloff said that the trading climate for the Aluminium and Plumbware division over the period, particularly in the first four months, was poor.
He said that in both market sectors competition was severe, paring margins in the face of weak demand.
The half-year also saw significant reduction in employment within the group and the consequent retrenchment packages contributed meaningful non-recurrent costs.
Eloff said that the total cost structure had been considerably reduced.
He said the recent sale of part of the Engineering division released funds which helped reduce the high level of the group's gearing.
"We are negotiating to dispose of the remaining non-core businesses and achievement of that should effectively remove gearing from the equation," Eloff said.
He said further restructuring was in progress.
